 Shri Sanjeev Neekhra - Advocate for the appellant
 Shri A.S. Parihar - Advocate for the respondents.

Order 
This appeal has been filed by the appellant Insurance Company under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 14.05.2024 passed by the 8th Additional Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Rewa in MACC No.400063/2016 whereby the learned MACT has awarded a sum of Rs.22,77,231/- along with interest @ 6% per annum to respondent Nos. 1 to 4, legal representatives of the deceased Mahendra Kumar Dwivedi who died in a road accident.

entities.text: 8th Additional Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Rewa
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts giving rise to the present appeal are that on 28.09.2015, when deceased Mahendra Kumar Dwivedi aged about 30 years was returning home along with his friend Avadesh Kumar in a motorcycle met with an accident.
The motorcycle was driven by the non- applicant No. 2 (in claim case) and the deceased was sitting as a pillion NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:42600 2 MA-6668-2024 rider.
The motorcycle was being driven at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, the motorcycle climbed a heap of mud and met with an accident and met with an accident.
As a result of which, the deceased Mahendra Kumar Dwivedi fell onto the road and sustained injury on head and became unconscious.

Thereafter, the deceased was admitted to S.G.M.
Hospital Rewa for treatment, where he died on 28.09.2015 during treatment.

3. It is not in dispute that the respondent no.6 was responsible for causing the accident and on the fateful day, the offending vehicle was insured with the present appellant.
4.

Learned counsel for the appellant contends that the only ground raised in this appeal is that the learned Tribunal has wrongly applied the method of calculation while assessing income under the head of future prospects.

It is contended by the counsel that the claimants/respondents have fairly The New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Sunita Dwivedi on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73160911/
1 admitted this facts.

sentences.text: However, the Tribunal, by mistake, applied an incorrect method for such calculation.
Accordingly, the only question for determination in this appeal is whether the method of calculation adopted by the Tribunal under the head of future prospects is proper or not.

5. Refuting the submissions made by learned counsel for the appellant, learned counsel for the respondents submitted that the findings arrived at by the learned Tribunal are just and proper and does not require any interference by this Court under this appeal.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:42600 3 MA-6668-2024 6.
Heard the submissions and perused the record.

7. On perusal of record it reflects that the annual income assessed by the learned Tribunal is not in dispute, therefore, this Court shall recalculate the awarded amount based on the same annual income.

The Tribunal has assessed the annual income of the deceased at Rs. 1,04,820/-.
8.
As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi , (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40% of the annual income is to be added towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi , (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, 40% of the annual income of Rs.1,04,820/- amounts to Rs. 41,928/-.
Thus, the total income, including future prospects, comes to Rs. 1,46,748/- (Rs. 1,04,820/- + Rs. 41,928/-).
9. In the present case, respondents No. 1 to 4 are the dependents of the deceased.

Therefore, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121, one-fourth (1/4th) of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

entities.text: Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After such deduction, the annual income comes to Rs. 1,10,061/- (i.e., Rs. 1,46,748/- minus 1/4th) and the multiplier of 17 is also applicable in the present case.

Accordingly, the compensation under the head of loss of dependency would be Rs.
18,71,037/- (Rs. 1,10,061  17)
10.
This Court is of the considered view that the annual income of the deceased shall be taken as Rs.1,46,748/-.

Deducting one-fourth of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:42600 4 MA-6668-2024 said amount, i.e., Rs. 36,687/-, towards personal and living expenses, the net annual income comes to Rs. 1,10,061/- (Rs. 1,46,748/- - Rs. 36,687/- = Rs. 1,10,061/-).

The learned Tribunal has properly assessed the awarded amounts under the heads of consortium, funeral expenses, and loss of estate at Rs. 1,92,000/-, Rs. 18,000/-, and Rs. 18,000/- respectively, and these amounts have not been disputed by any of the parties.

11. Consequently, the appeal filed by the Insurance Company is partly allowed in above terms and the amount of compensation is reduced as under :-

13. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the reduced amount of Rs.20,99,037/- (after adjusting any amount already paid) with accrued interest before the learned Tribunal.
14. The appellant/Insurance Co. is directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of 30 days from the date of this order, failing which the execution can be taken out against it.

16. The impugned award of the learned Tribunal stands modified to the aforesaid extent and in terms and directions as above.
17. The record be sent back to the learned Tribunal within two weeks from this day.
18. As a sequel, interlocutory applications pending consideration, if any, shall stand closed.
